title: Critical factors influencing the photodegradation of polyethylene: a comprehensive review
content: Photodegradation plays a critical role in the environmental breakdown of polyethylene (PE), which is a plastic known for its large-scale production and long-lasting nature. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the mechanisms and key factors influencing the photodegradation of PE, including polymer structure, the presence of additives, temperature, and environmental factors such as humidity. Photodegradation of PE is primarily driven by photooxidation; hence, oxygen availability and proper photon energy can enhance the degradation rate. PE with more amorphous regions and lower molecular weight is more prone to chain scission, accelerating degradation. The interaction among these variables shapes the degradation behavior, mechanism, and the formation of oxidation products. This review highlights the role of additives, particularly photocatalysts, in modulating PE's susceptibility to UV-induced degradation. Analytical techniques such as Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, thermal, and mechanical analysis are discussed as key analytical tools for assessing polymer changes in PE during photodegradation. Despite numerous publications, many details remain poorly understood regarding the controlling factors and mechanisms of PE photodegradation under environmental conditions.
